nodes.label: Storage Driver (local disk / S3 stub)
nodes.rationale: The local driver writes to disk, which an ephemeral container will lose; the S3 adapter must be finished before production.

nodes.label: check_imports.py
nodes.community_name: Redesign Verification Suite (control-label regression, 133 logic tests, WCAG matrix)
nodes.rationale: Verifies all local imports resolve across 175 files on every redesign round.

nodes.label: detect.mjs (slop detector)
nodes.community_name: Redesign Verification Suite (control-label regression, 133 logic tests, WCAG matrix)
nodes.rationale: Caught bounce easing on the coin pop, transition:width on the meter fill, and the 3px rarity side-rail as recognisable generated-interface tells.

nodes.label: Redesign Verification Suite (control-label regression, 133 logic tests, WCAG matrix)
nodes.community_name: Redesign Verification Suite (control-label regression, 133 logic tests, WCAG matrix)
nodes.norm_label: redesign verification suite (control-label regression, 133 logic tests, wcag matrix)
nodes.rationale: A 116-item control-label regression proved no feature was lost, 133 logic tests confirmed the economy/SRS/marking/timezone/anti-cheat rules were unchanged, and a WCAG contrast matrix verified all 136 colour x surface pairs clear AA in both themes.

nodes.label: Static Harness Flattered the Build
nodes.rationale: The screenshot harness hand-authored one of each rarity onto dashboard cards while the real page hardcoded every item to common; fixed by making the harness compute rarity with the same two rules as the app. Sample data may stand in for a query; it may never stand in for a derivation.

nodes.label: Skeleton Shaped Like the Page
nodes.rationale: A skeleton that does not occupy the same box as the real content is decoration; the page still jumps when data lands, so every route's loading.tsx must be shaped like the page it stands in for.

nodes.label: Technical Gotchas (theme inline, Tailwind scan, heartbeat deps)
nodes.norm_label: technical gotchas (theme inline, tailwind scan, heartbeat deps)
nodes.rationale: @theme inline does not emit real CSS custom properties; Tailwind only generates classes present as literal source text, so template-interpolated class names silently fail; and putting pathname in the heartbeat effect's deps rebuilds it on every navigation, producing a wave of 429s.

nodes.label: Navigation Slowness Fix (NavigationProvider)
nodes.rationale: next dev disables prefetch so loading.tsx boundaries never show; the real fix holds the pending destination in a capture-phase listener with a CSS-hidden sibling skeleton, since a component cannot commit a state change while its own subtree is suspended.

nodes.label: requireUser() authorisation boundary
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Called before any child page renders in the (app) layout, so no feature page has to remember to check; every service query is additionally scoped by ownership or membership.

nodes.label: The Rarity Frame (signature component)
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: The one irreducible component: a card whose cut edge and inset keyline carry the rarity its content earned, with foil at the top step, letting a library read as a collection at a glance.

nodes.label: Daily Quiz
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Attempting it, not passing it, is what extends the streak.

nodes.label: Product Purpose: Measurable Progression
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: StudyQuest turns revision into measurable progression; success is a student choosing to open it on a day nobody told them to revise.

nodes.label: Smart Mode (Spaced Repetition Scheduler)
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed

nodes.label: Study Coins (earned currency)
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Coins come from finishing sets, quiz scores, the daily quiz and verified study time; a competitor can copy points and badges but not a progression system validated server-side against measured activity.

nodes.label: Cram Mode
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Cram reviews are recorded but never touch Smart Mode scheduling, so cramming before a test can't wreck a carefully built long-term schedule.

nodes.label: Server-Measured Heartbeat Time
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Elapsed time is min(now - storedLastHeartbeat, 45s) computed on the server's clock; replaying the request credits zero and disappearing for an hour credits only one interval.

nodes.label: Append-Only Ledger with Idempotency Key
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: A double-submit violates a unique index and awards nothing; User.coinBalance is a cache of SUM(ledger.amount) reconciled by a worker.

nodes.label: Adaptive Spaced Repetition Intervals
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed

nodes.label: The Amber Rule
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Amber means Study Coins and legendary mastery only; a streak, score, card count or timer never takes gold, keeping the currency colour meaningful.

nodes.label: The Earned-Foil Rule
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Foil is the system's one material effect and appears only at legendary rank; adding it elsewhere spends the only currency the visual system has.

nodes.label: Amber Means Money
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: coin and legendary share a hue deliberately, but amber on any figure means it is literally Study Coins; a streak is coral because a run of days is not a balance.

nodes.label: Foil Is Earned-Only
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Foil appears only on legendary and is never decoration; if adding foil is only to make something look good, the answer is no.

nodes.label: Hard Constraints (server-validated rewards)
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Every reward calculation is validated server-side and study time is measured between server heartbeats; the frontend must never be trusted to decide whether a student has earned coins.

nodes.label: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.norm_label: why the coin economy can't be farmed
nodes.rationale: Ten enumerated safeguards (single mutator, idempotent ledger, one transaction, measured not reported time, server-issued deadlines, server-side marking, override doesn't pay, verified completion, DB-read limits, timezone-change caps) ensure nothing trusts the browser.

nodes.label: The Layering Rule (pages -> actions -> services)
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Pages and components never touch the database; server actions validate and rate-limit, services own business rules and transactions, and pure logic has no I/O so it can be tested exhaustively.

nodes.label: Decision: MCQ Marked Deterministically, Not by AI
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.norm_label: decision: mcq marked deterministically, not by ai
nodes.rationale: Multiple choice is exact-match, so AI marking would be slower, cost money, and could only make it worse.

nodes.label: The Struggle Detector
nodes.community_name: Why the Coin Economy Can't Be Farmed
nodes.rationale: Three failures in the last four reviews floors the interval at 12 hours; it deliberately never fires on a correct answer, because pinning a recovering card to 12h would stop it ever escaping.

nodes.label: accentFor() (deprecated hash-to-hue helper)
nodes.rationale: A vestige of the previous (Ink & Gold) system that assigns decorative per-item colour by hashing a string; directly contradicts the Rarity Rule and must not be wired to anything.

nodes.label: The Collector's Table (Creative North Star)
nodes.rationale: StudyQuest is a collection, not a dashboard; the interface refuses both the gamified card-grid cliche and the monochrome product-tool clone by making colour a claim about earned mastery rather than decoration.

nodes.label: Arena Placeholder Routes
nodes.rationale: The six Arena routes are deliberate non-functional placeholders that must stay visible but must not claim to work, per the user's request that the Arena remain a quiet door rather than a headline.

nodes.label: The Earned-Stock Rule
nodes.rationale: Card stock represents real, studied material; an unbuilt feature (the Arena) gets no frame at all, because giving it card stock would be a quiet door claiming to be furniture.

nodes.label: The Frame-Carries-Rarity Rule
nodes.rationale: Rarity is printed into the cut edge and inset keyline, never a coloured stripe/rail/bar, because a coloured side stripe above 1px is the single most recognisable tell of a generated interface; on a real trading card the frame itself is the rarity.

nodes.label: The Ink Variant Rule
nodes.rationale: Plain coral measures 3.01:1 on the table and fails AA for anything but large text, so any rarity hue used as text must switch to its -ink variant.

nodes.label: Rarity Is Mastery (semantic colour scale)
nodes.rationale: A hue on the surface is always a claim about what a student has earned; this is what makes the palette semantic rather than merely pretty, and is derived by a single function rather than assigned by hand.

nodes.label: The Frame Carries the Rarity, Not a Stripe
nodes.norm_label: the frame carries the rarity, not a stripe
nodes.rationale: A 3px coloured side rail was the first draft; the craft floor refused any coloured border above 1px as one of the most recognisable tells of a generated interface.

nodes.label: Stock Means Earned
nodes.rationale: Card stock is what the product's real material sits on; an unbuilt feature (the Arena) is a hairline strip on the table, never a Panel.

nodes.label: Product Principles
nodes.rationale: Earned-not-awarded, next-action-beats-summary, solo-revision-is-the-product, honest-about-what-is-not-built, and the student's-day-not-the-server's — five commitments the product must not violate.

nodes.label: Card Frames (design system name)
nodes.rationale: Replaces 'Ink & Gold', the previous monochrome graphite-and-gold system; nothing in Card Frames is inherited from it unless stated.

nodes.label: Legacy Token Aliases (violet/cyan/lime/rose/amber/panel)
nodes.rationale: Repointed rather than renamed so roughly 174 files could re-theme from one file with no chance of a screen being missed; treated as read-only compatibility, never extended.

nodes.label: Card Frames Redesign Round
nodes.rationale: A complete visual rebuild run through the impeccable skill; picked by Louis from a dealt hand of seven candidates (seed f2d16265), with no functionality removed.

nodes.label: Impeccable Skill (redesign methodology)
nodes.rationale: The redesign was run through this skill rather than by taste, driving the brief and the verification steps used on every round.

nodes.label: Ink & Gold (previous design system)
nodes.rationale: The monochrome graphite-and-gold scheme that Card Frames replaced entirely, not layered over.

nodes.label: StatStrip Component
nodes.rationale: How any screen summarises a thing as one divided panel rather than four separate cards, because four cards say 'unrelated numbers' while one divided frame says 'the state of this thing'.

nodes.label: The Measurement Rule
nodes.rationale: Any coin, timer, score or count takes tabular lining numerals (.num) so a ticking value never nudges layout.

nodes.label: The Pip-and-Total Rule
nodes.rationale: Large numerals are reserved for the four StatStrip totals; everything else is a struck pip, because seven label-plus-big-number cells stacked together is the hero-metric scaffold the product refuses.

nodes.label: The Hue-Is-Never-The-Only-Signal Rule
nodes.rationale: No state is announced by colour alone, because the audience includes younger teenagers and phone-first readers, so every colour-coded state carries a second cue (underline, label, hatch, words).

nodes.label: The Icon Weight Rule
nodes.rationale: Bold icons for actions/navigation, fill icons for things owned/earned, because solid glyphs read as objects and outlined glyphs read as actions in a collection-based product.

nodes.label: The Next-Action-First Rule
nodes.rationale: The first viewport puts the decision of what to study now before any summary, total or history.

nodes.label: The No-Kicker Rule
nodes.rationale: No small-caps/uppercase kicker sits above a heading; a heading must carry its own weight.

nodes.label: The One Primary Rule
nodes.rationale: Only one primary (brushed-sheen) button may be in view, so the main action stays unmistakable without being the loudest object on screen.

nodes.label: The Real-Offset Rule
nodes.rationale: Every shadow has a real vertical offset and warm tint; zero-offset halos or coloured glows read as a screenshot pasted onto the table.

nodes.label: The Struck-and-Read Rule
nodes.rationale: Archivo carries anything struck (headings, titles, numbers) and Schibsted Grotesk carries anything read, keeping typographic roles unambiguous.

nodes.label: The Two-Value Ground Rule
nodes.rationale: Only table and stock exist as grounds, both warm (R>G>B) in both themes, because a neutral grey anywhere turns the product back into a form.

nodes.label: Neon DB Password Leak (unrotated)
nodes.rationale: The Neon database password pasted into chat earlier should still be rotated — a standing, unresolved security exposure flagged in the notes.

nodes.label: Communities
nodes.rationale: Communities exist to move material between students, not to become a feed to scroll.
